title: Had we known…
goal: Review an outcome without confusing hindsight, warnings and established causes

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The late opening
paragraphs: Guests arrived before the doors opened, but the sound test had not been completed. The event eventually started twelve minutes late. The opening log records both problems, without identifying who knew about them or when they were told.

Two explanations remain under review: insufficient preparation time and a warning that may not have reached the right person. The message record has not yet been checked, so the log alone does not establish which explanation caused the delay.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: A guest’s account
paragraphs: While waiting, one guest heard two different updates. A volunteer said the event would start soon; another said a technical check was still in progress. Neither update explained how long the wait would be.
The guest wanted a short, accurate update rather than reassurance that kept changing. They could describe what the volunteers said, but they could not identify who controlled the opening decision.

questions.prompt: Why might a checkpoint alone be insufficient?
questions.answer: Someone must own the decision triggered by the checkpoint
Kim proposes naming a decision-maker with authority to delay opening

questions.answer: Their causal conclusion remains provisional until the evidence is checked

pages.title: Judge what was foreseeable
pages.instruction: Review the event log and guest report with Teacher. Separate what is known from what still needs checking

pages.title: Invert had in a third conditional
pages.instruction: Drop if and move had before the subject for a more formal unreal past condition

rows.subject: With if
rows.verb: If + subject + had + participle, could / would have + participle
rows.example: If we had tested earlier, we could have found the problem

rows.subject: Inversion without if
rows.verb: Had + subject + participle, could / would have + participle
rows.example: Had we tested earlier, we could have found the problem

rows.subject: Negative inversion
rows.example: Had we not checked the sound, we might have missed the problem

pages.note: The meaning remains an unreal past condition. Inversion changes order and register; it does not prove what caused the actual delay.

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: A warning existed, but who owned it? Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I found the missing message record. A warning that the sound test was incomplete was sent before the planned opening time, but it went to a shared group without a named person responsible for responding. There’s no acknowledgement in the record. That makes a communication failure more plausible than simply saying nobody noticed a problem. It still doesn’t establish whether enough testing time had been scheduled, or whether a recipient read the warning and chose not to act. Could you revise the review to reflect that distinction? I’d like one preventive action linked to what we can actually establish, rather than a general instruction to be more careful. If you use “Had we known”, please make clear whose knowledge you mean
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. I found the missing message record. A warning that the sound test was incomplete was sent before the planned opening time, but it went to a shared group without a named person responsible for responding. There’s no acknowledgement in the record. That makes a communication failure more plausible than simply saying nobody noticed a problem. It still doesn’t establish whether enough testing time had been scheduled, or whether a recipient read the warning and chose not to act. Could you revise the review to reflect that distinction? I’d like one preventive action linked to what we can actually establish, rather than a general instruction to be more careful. If you use “Had we known”, please make clear whose knowledge you mean.
pages.greeting: There’s a useful distinction in the update

s_mission.title: Opening review

questions.prompt: Which two problems does the opening log confirm?
questions.answer: The sound test was incomplete, and the event started twelve minutes late.
questions.hint: Look at the two outcomes in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Which two explanations is the review considering?
questions.answer: It is considering insufficient preparation time and a warning that failed to reach the right person.
questions.hint: Find the two explanations at the start of paragraph two.

questions.prompt: What evidence has not yet been checked?
questions.answer: The message record has not yet been checked.
questions.hint: Look for the record mentioned in the final sentence.

referenceParagraphs: The opening log records an incomplete sound test and a twelve-minute delay. Guests had already arrived before the doors opened. It does not record when the team first learnt that testing was unfinished.

The review is considering insufficient preparation time and a warning that failed to reach the right person. The message record has not yet been checked; neither explanation has been confirmed as the cause.

s_reply.title: What the message record shows

questions.answer: The warning was sent before the doors opened.
questions.hint: Compare the warning with the opening time.

questions.prompt: Which two follow-up details are missing from the record?
questions.answer: No responder was named, and there is no recorded acknowledgement.
questions.hint: Look for who was responsible and whether receipt was confirmed.

questions.prompt: Why does the record not establish that someone ignored the warning?
questions.answer: It does not identify who read the message.
questions.hint: Find the missing evidence about receipt.

referenceParagraphs: The message record shows that a warning was sent before the doors opened. However, no responder was named, and there is no recorded acknowledgement of the warning.

The record does not identify who read the message or whether enough time remained to complete the test. It therefore establishes that a warning was sent, but not that a particular person received and ignored it.
